name: Architecture Synchronization & Versioning Loop
description: Iterative loop to synchronize architecture with implementation reality when drift is detected
new_in_version: Reflow v3.15.0 - Architecture Synchronization Loop feature
purpose: Ensure architecture documents always reflect implementation reality through systematic synchronization and versioning
rationale: Development and testing iterations cause implementation to diverge from designed architecture due to requirements creep, performance optimization, and operational realities. This step provides a systematic mechanism to detect drift, classify root causes, update architecture with versioning, and verify synchronization.
when_to_execute: After D-06 (As-Built Architecture Generation) and before D-07 (Pre-Deployment Validation)

actions.name: Analyze Architecture Delta Significance
actions.description: Determine severity of architectural drift from D-06 delta report

extract_from_delta_report.similarity_score: Overall Jaccard similarity between designed and built architecture
extract_from_delta_report.breaking_changes: List of breaking changes (service removals, interface changes)

similarity_score >= 0.95.interpretation: Implementation matches design very closely (95%+ match)
similarity_score >= 0.95.action: Document minor deltas in rationale file, proceed to D-07
similarity_score >= 0.95.llm_guidance: Skip to D-06.5-A09 (document and complete step)

0.7 <= similarity_score < 0.95.action: REVIEW REQUIRED - decide whether to update architecture OR fix implementation
review_criteria: Do changes improve the system (performance, security, maintainability)?

similarity_score < 0.7.interpretation: Significant drift (<70% match) - implementation substantially different from design
similarity_score < 0.7.action: MANDATORY SYNCHRONIZATION - must update architecture OR fix implementation before proceeding
similarity_score < 0.7.llm_guidance: Proceed to D-06.5-A02 (classify root causes), synchronization is REQUIRED
similarity_score < 0.7.enforcement: Gate G-D-06.5 will BLOCK if drift remains unresolved

actions.output: Console summary of drift severity and required action

actions.name: Root Cause Classification
actions.description: Classify why architecture diverged from design to track patterns and guide decision
actions.purpose: Understanding root cause helps decide whether to update architecture or fix implementation
llm_instructions: Review the delta report from D-06-A02
For each significant change, determine the most likely root cause
Consider development history, test results, performance data
Classify into one or more categories below

requirements_creep.description: New or changed requirements discovered during implementation/testing
examples: Stakeholder requested additional functionality during development
Discovered missing use cases during integration testing
Integration with external system revealed new requirements
Compliance requirements discovered during security review
requirements_creep.recommended_action: Update functional architecture AND service architecture to reflect validated new requirements

performance_optimization.description: Original design could not meet performance requirements
examples: Synchronous design too slow, switched to async processing
Database schema caused slow queries, redesigned indexes/schema
Memory consumption too high, refactored to streaming
Network latency required caching layer not in original design
Batch processing too slow, added parallel processing
indicators_in_delta: Added load balancers or scaling components
performance_optimization.recommended_action: Update service architecture to reflect optimized design (functional architecture may not change)

technical_constraints.description: Design was impossible or impractical to implement due to technical limitations
examples: Library/framework limitations not known during design
Deployment environment constraints (e.g., database permissions)
Technology stack incompatibilities
Cloud provider limitations
Container orchestration constraints
indicators_in_delta: Changed technology choices (different database, message queue, etc.)
Simplified service boundaries due to technology limits
technical_constraints.recommended_action: Update service architecture, document constraints in architecture notes

security_hardening.description: Security requirements not fully addressed in original design
examples: Added authentication layer not in original design
Added authorization service for fine-grained access control
Added encryption for data at rest/in transit
Added audit logging service
Added API gateway for rate limiting and security
indicators_in_delta: Changed interface contracts to include auth tokens
security_hardening.recommended_action: Update service architecture to reflect security enhancements

examples: Database permissions prevented designed approach, used alternative
Network topology required different service layout
Scaling requirements changed service boundaries
Monitoring/observability requirements added services
Cost optimization changed infrastructure design
operational_reality.recommended_action: Update service architecture, document operational constraints

developer_mistake.description: Implementation deviated from design unintentionally (oversight or misunderstanding)
examples: Misunderstood architecture specifications
Forgot to implement designed features
Implemented wrong interface contract
Missed services or interfaces in implementation
developer_mistake.recommended_action: FIX IMPLEMENTATION to match design (do NOT update architecture)

root_causes.rationale: Operational testing revealed 45s character generation time, redesigned to async
affected_changes: Changed CharacterService → AttributeService interface to async message-based
Added async processing functions to functional architecture

llm_instructions_detailed: For each category, assess if it applies to the observed drift
Assign confidence level: high, medium, low
Provide clear rationale linking delta changes to root cause
List specific changes affected by this root cause
Include evidence (test results, stakeholder feedback, technical docs)
Multiple root causes are possible (e.g., both performance + security)

actions.name: Architecture Update Decision
actions.description: Decide whether to update architecture or fix implementation based on root cause analysis

update_architecture_if: Root cause is requirements_creep AND new requirements are validated by stakeholders
Root cause is performance_optimization AND optimization is validated through testing
Root cause is technical_constraints AND constraints are real/documented
Root cause is security_hardening AND security requirements are validated
Root cause is operational_reality AND constraints are unavoidable/documented
fix_implementation_if: Root cause is developer_mistake (always fix code, not architecture)
Changes introduce unnecessary complexity or technical debt
Original design is superior and implementation should match
Changes violate security, quality, or architectural standards
Changes were made without proper justification
hybrid_approach: Some changes are legitimate (update architecture for these)
Some changes are mistakes (fix implementation for these)

user_prompt.question: Architecture diverged from design (similarity: {score}). Root cause: {categories}. How should we proceed?
options: Update architecture to match implementation (validated changes)
Fix implementation to match architecture (unintentional deviation)
Hybrid: Update some aspects of architecture, fix others (RECOMMENDED for moderate drift)

show_details.root_cause_analysis: Display categories with confidence and rationale

llm_guidance: For developer_mistake: ALWAYS recommend fixing implementation
For performance_optimization with test evidence: USUALLY recommend updating architecture
For requirements_creep: Verify with user that requirements are validated, then update architecture
For moderate drift (0.7-0.95): Hybrid approach is usually best
For major drift (<0.7): Likely multiple root causes, need comprehensive review

actions.name: Version and Update Architecture Specifications
actions.description: Update architecture files with versioning and rationale using version_architecture.py tool
actions.conditional: Only if D-06.5-A03 decision includes architecture updates

steps.step: 1. Determine which architecture files to update
steps.guidance: Based on D-06.5-A03 decision, identify files that need updates
Edit architecture JSON files to reflect implementation reality
llm_instructions: Use Edit tool to update architecture files
Add new services, interfaces, or functions as needed
Update existing definitions to match implementation
Ensure JSON schema validity after edits
Document changes clearly in commit messages

steps.purpose: Create versioned snapshots and update version history
steps.example: python3 {reflow_root}/tools/version_architecture.py --system-root {system_root} --change-type performance_optimization --rationale "Redesigned for async processing due to 45s latency in operational testing" --similarity-score 0.62 --changed-files "service_architecture.json,functional_architecture.json" --triggered-by "D-06.5"

version_increment_rules.major: Breaking changes (interface contract changes, service removal) - increments major version
version_increment_rules.minor: Non-breaking additions (new endpoints, new services) - increments minor version
version_increment_rules.patch: Internal changes (performance optimization, refactoring) - increments patch version

actions.name: Re-validate Updated Architecture
actions.description: Ensure updated architecture is still valid, complete, and internally consistent
validation_checks: No orphaned interfaces (interfaces not used by any service)
Functional flows still valid (if functional_architecture.json updated)

on_failure.action: Fix architecture validation errors before proceeding
on_failure.guidance: Common validation errors after architecture updates:
common_errors: Interface added to service but not in interface_registry.json - add to registry
Service references interface that doesn't exist - create ICD for interface
Circular dependencies introduced - review service dependencies
Missing required fields in service_architecture.json - add missing fields

actions.success_criteria: validate_architecture.py exits with success (exit code 0, no errors)

actions.name: Regenerate Architecture Artifacts
actions.description: Regenerate all derived artifacts from updated architecture specifications
actions.purpose: Keep all architecture representations (graphs, diagrams, docs) synchronized with updated specs

artifacts_to_regenerate.purpose: Master graph representation of system architecture

artifacts_to_regenerate.conditional: Only if project uses language-native contracts (v3.10.0 feature)

llm_instructions: Run tools in order listed above
Check that each tool completes successfully
Verify generated artifacts are valid (JSON parseable, diagrams renderable)
If any tool fails, fix the issue before proceeding

actions.name: Verify Architecture Synchronization
actions.description: Generate new as-built architecture and compare to updated as-designed to verify synchronization
actions.purpose: Prove that architecture now matches implementation (similarity should be >= 0.95)
process: 1. Re-generate as-built architecture from current implementation (may have changed if D-06.5-A08 ran)
2. Compare as-built to updated as-designed architecture

success_criteria.rationale: After synchronization, as-built and as-designed should match very closely (95%+)
success_criteria.acceptable_remaining_drift: Minor implementation details (comments, internal refactorings) may still differ

loop_condition.then: Review remaining differences - may need another iteration
actions: Determine if remaining differences are acceptable or need resolution
If not acceptable: Return to D-06.5-A03 (decide update vs fix)
If acceptable: Document rationale and proceed

actions.on_max_iterations: If still not synchronized after 3 iterations, escalate to human review - may need fundamental redesign

actions.name: Update Implementation (If Needed)
actions.description: If decision was to fix implementation, update code to match designed architecture
actions.conditional: Only if D-06.5-A03 decision was 'fix_implementation' or 'hybrid' with implementation fixes needed
actions.purpose: Correct implementation deviations so code matches intended design

process.step: 1. Review implementation fixes from D-06.5-A03 decision
2. Identify code files that deviate from architecture
methods: Review delta report to see what's missing or wrong

process.step: 3. Update implementation to match designed architecture
examples: Implement missing endpoints specified in ICDs
Remove services that were added by mistake
Fix interface contracts to match ICDs
Correct service responsibilities per architecture

actions.feedback_loop: This action creates iteration: fix code → re-validate → re-generate as-built → verify synchronization
actions.note: May need multiple iterations if fixes introduce new issues

actions.name: Document Synchronization Completion
actions.description: Create final documentation of architecture synchronization process and outcome
actions.purpose: Provide clear record of what changed, why, and that architecture is now synchronized

signoff_format.acceptable_remaining_drift: Minor internal refactorings, no functional differences

gates.name: Architecture Synchronization Gate
checks: Architecture delta analyzed and classified by root cause (D-06.5-A01, D-06.5-A02)
Decision made: update architecture OR fix implementation (D-06.5-A03)
If similarity < 0.7: Synchronization actions COMPLETED (architecture updated OR implementation fixed)
If similarity 0.7-0.95: Review completed and documented
If architecture updated: Updated architecture re-validated successfully (D-06.5-A05)
If architecture updated: All artifacts regenerated (D-06.5-A06)
Changes versioned with rationale in architecture_version_history.json (D-06.5-A04)

enforcement.similarity < 0.7: BLOCKING - MUST synchronize (update architecture or fix implementation) before proceeding to D-07
enforcement.similarity 0.7-0.95: BLOCKING - MUST review, decide, and document before proceeding
enforcement.similarity >= 0.95: NON-BLOCKING - document minimal drift and proceed

gates.bypass_not_allowed: This gate enforces architectural discipline - cannot be bypassed

typical_time.major_drift (< 0.7): 3-6 hours (comprehensive synchronization, may require multiple iterations)

critical_reminders: This step is the KEY to keeping architecture synchronized with implementation
DO NOT skip this step even if drift seems acceptable - documentation is important
For similarity < 0.7: Synchronization is MANDATORY, not optional
Always version architecture changes using version_architecture.py tool
Re-validate architecture after updates (D-06.5-A05 is critical)
Verify synchronization with new as-built comparison (D-06.5-A07)

decision_making_guidance.developer_mistake: ALWAYS fix implementation, never update architecture
decision_making_guidance.performance_optimization: Usually update architecture IF validated by testing
decision_making_guidance.requirements_creep: Update architecture IF new requirements validated by stakeholders
decision_making_guidance.technical_constraints: Update architecture IF constraints are real and documented
decision_making_guidance.when_in_doubt: Ask user via user_prompt in D-06.5-A03

common_pitfalls: Not re-validating after architecture updates - always run validate_architecture.py
Not regenerating artifacts - architecture and graphs will be out of sync
Accepting high drift without synchronization - enforces poor discipline
